uses: Relief of mild to moderate pain including headache, toothache, muscle pain, backache, and menstrual pain. Also used to reduce fever (antipyretic).
side_effects: Common: Nausea, stomach pain, loss of appetite. Rare but serious: Skin rash, itching, hives, allergic reactions (swelling of face/lips/tongue), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, liver damage with overdose. If you develop a rash after taking Dolo 650, stop the medication immediately and consult a doctor as it may indicate an allergic reaction to paracetamol.
dosage: Adults: 1 tablet every 4-6 hours as needed. Maximum 4 tablets (2600mg) in 24 hours. Do not exceed recommended dose.
warnings: Do not take more than 4g of paracetamol in 24 hours. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Not recommended for patients with severe liver disease. If rash or allergic symptoms develop, discontinue immediately and seek medical attention.
interactions: Warfarin (increased bleeding risk), alcohol (increased liver damage risk), other paracetamol-containing products (risk of overdose), carbamazepine, isoniazid.

uses: Relief of pain (headache, toothache, body ache) and fever. Also used for cold and flu symptoms.
side_effects: Common: Nausea, stomach upset. Rare: Allergic reactions (rash, itching, swelling), liver damage with overdose, blood disorders (thrombocytopenia).
dosage: Adults: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours. Maximum 8 tablets of 500mg or 6 tablets of 650mg in 24 hours.
warnings: Do not exceed recommended dose. Avoid with alcohol. Consult doctor if symptoms persist for more than 3 days.
interactions: Warfarin, alcohol, other paracetamol products, metoclopramide.

uses: Pain relief for headache, dental pain, muscle pain, joint pain, menstrual cramps, backache, and fever.
side_effects: Common: Stomach pain, nausea, heartburn, dizziness. Serious: GI bleeding, ulcers, kidney problems, allergic reactions, skin rash, increased blood pressure, cardiovascular events.
dosage: Adults: 1 tablet 2-3 times daily after food. Do not exceed 3 tablets per day.
warnings: Take with food to reduce stomach irritation. Not recommended for patients with peptic ulcers, kidney disease, or heart failure. Avoid in third trimester of pregnancy.
interactions: Aspirin, anticoagulants, lithium, methotrexate, ACE inhibitors, diuretics.

uses: Bacterial infections including respiratory tract infections (pneumonia, bronchitis), ear infections, skin infections, sexually transmitted infections (chlamydia), and certain eye infections.
side_effects: Common: Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting. Rare: Liver problems, QT prolongation, hearing loss, allergic reactions, Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea.
dosage: Adults: Usually 500mg once daily for 3 days, or 500mg on day 1 followed by 250mg daily for days 2-5.
warnings: Complete the full course even if feeling better. May cause QT prolongation - caution with heart conditions. Inform doctor about liver disease.
interactions: Antacids (take 1 hour before or 2 hours after), warfarin, cyclosporine, digoxin.

uses: Bacterial infections including ear infections, pneumonia, skin infections, urinary tract infections, H. pylori (with other drugs), dental infections, and tonsillitis.
side_effects: Common: Diarrhea, nausea, rash, vomiting. Serious: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) especially in penicillin-allergic patients, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, liver problems, seizures at high doses.
dosage: Adults: 250-500mg every 8 hours or 500-875mg every 12 hours depending on infection severity.
warnings: Tell your doctor if allergic to penicillin or cephalosporins. Complete the full course of treatment. May reduce effectiveness of oral contraceptives.
interactions: Methotrexate, warfarin, probenecid, oral contraceptives.

uses: Allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes), chronic urticaria (hives), skin allergies, itching, and allergic skin rashes.
side_effects: Common: Drowsiness, dry mouth, fatigue, headache. Uncommon: Dizziness, stomach pain, diarrhea. Rare: Palpitations, urinary retention.
dosage: Adults: 10mg once daily. Can be taken with or without food.
warnings: May cause drowsiness - avoid driving. Use with caution in kidney disease. Avoid alcohol.
interactions: Alcohol (increased sedation), CNS depressants, theophylline.

uses: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, prevention of NSAID-induced ulcers, H. pylori eradication (with antibiotics).
side_effects: Common: Headache, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, flatulence. Long-term: Vitamin B12 deficiency, magnesium deficiency, increased fracture risk, C. difficile infection.
dosage: Adults: 40mg once daily before breakfast for 4-8 weeks.
warnings: Not for immediate heartburn relief. Long-term use may increase risk of bone fractures and magnesium deficiency. May mask symptoms of gastric cancer.
interactions: Atazanavir, clopidogrel, methotrexate, ketoconazole, iron supplements.

uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy or in combination. Also used for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and insulin resistance.
side_effects: Common: Nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, metallic taste, decreased appetite. Serious: Lactic acidosis (rare but life-threatening), vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use.
dosage: Adults: Start with 500mg twice daily with meals. May increase gradually to max 2550mg/day in divided doses.
warnings: Take with food to reduce GI side effects. Stop before contrast dye procedures. Not for type 1 diabetes. Monitor kidney function regularly. Avoid excessive alcohol.
interactions: Alcohol, contrast dyes (iodinated), carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, cimetidine.

uses: High blood pressure (hypertension), coronary artery disease, angina (chest pain), Raynaud's phenomenon.
side_effects: Common: Ankle swelling (edema), dizziness, flushing, headache, fatigue. Uncommon: Palpitations, nausea, abdominal pain. Rare: Gum hyperplasia, liver problems.
dosage: Adults: Start 5mg once daily. May increase to 10mg once daily. Can be taken with or without food.
warnings: Do not stop suddenly. May cause excessive blood pressure drop in severe aortic stenosis. Use with caution in heart failure and liver disease.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin), simvastatin (limit to 20mg), cyclosporine, tacrolimus.

uses: High cholesterol (hypercholesterolemia), high triglycerides, prevention of cardiovascular disease, reduction of heart attack and stroke risk.
side_effects: Common: Muscle pain (myalgia), joint pain, diarrhea, nausea. Serious: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle breakdown), liver damage, new-onset diabetes. Rare: Memory problems.
dosage: Adults: Start 10-20mg once daily. May increase to max 80mg daily.
warnings: Report unexplained muscle pain immediately. Monitor liver function. Avoid grapefruit juice. Not for use in pregnancy or breastfeeding.
interactions: Cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, niacin, erythromycin, azole antifungals, grapefruit juice, warfarin.

uses: GERD, peptic ulcers, H. pylori eradication, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, erosive esophagitis.
side_effects: Common: Headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, gas. Long-term risks: Bone fractures, magnesium deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, C. difficile infection, kidney problems.
dosage: Adults: 20mg once daily before breakfast for 4-8 weeks. For severe: 40mg daily.
warnings: Best taken 30-60 minutes before first meal. Not intended for long-term use without doctor supervision.
interactions: Clopidogrel (reduces effectiveness), diazepam, warfarin, phenytoin, methotrexate, tacrolimus.

uses: Asthma prevention and chronic treatment, allergic rhinitis, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction prevention.
side_effects: Common: Headache, stomach pain, heartburn, tiredness. Serious: Neuropsychiatric events (mood changes, depression, suicidal thoughts, anxiety, insomnia, hallucinations, aggression). FDA boxed warning for mental health side effects.
dosage: Adults: 10mg once daily in the evening.
warnings: FDA BLACK BOX WARNING: Risk of neuropsychiatric events including suicidal thoughts. Not for acute asthma attacks. Monitor for behavioral changes.
interactions: Phenobarbital, rifampin, gemfibrozil.

uses: High blood pressure (hypertension), diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes, stroke risk reduction in patients with hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy.
side_effects: Common: Dizziness, upper respiratory infection, nasal congestion, back pain. Serious: Hyperkalemia (high potassium), kidney impairment, angioedema, hypotension.
dosage: Adults: Start 50mg once daily. Range 25-100mg daily in 1-2 doses.
warnings: Do NOT use in pregnancy (can cause fetal harm). Monitor potassium levels. May cause first-dose hypotension in volume-depleted patients.
interactions: Potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, lithium, rifampin.

uses: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid), TSH suppression for thyroid cancer, myxedema coma.
side_effects: At correct dose: Generally well tolerated. Overdose symptoms: Rapid heartbeat, chest pain, tremor, weight loss, insomnia, sweating, diarrhea, headache, nervousness.
dosage: Adults: Start 25-50 mcg daily. Adjust based on TSH levels every 6-8 weeks. Take on empty stomach 30-60 minutes before breakfast.
warnings: Take consistently on empty stomach. Not for weight loss. TSH monitoring required. Significant drug interactions - separate from many medications by 4 hours.
interactions: Calcium, iron, antacids (take 4 hours apart), warfarin, digoxin, estrogen, carbamazepine, rifampin, soy products.

uses: Pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, dental pain, menstrual pain, muscle pain, sports injuries, gout.
side_effects: Common: Stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, rash. Serious: GI bleeding/ulcers, cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke), kidney damage, liver problems, severe skin reactions.
dosage: Adults: 50mg 2-3 times daily or 75mg twice daily. Take with food.
warnings: Increased cardiovascular risk with long-term use. Take shortest duration at lowest dose. Not for use before or after CABG surgery. NSAID allergy risk.
interactions: Aspirin, anticoagulants (warfarin), lithium, methotrexate, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, SSRIs, corticosteroids.
available_forms: Tablet (25mg, 50mg), SR tablet (100mg), Gel, Injection, Suppository

uses: Pain relief, fever reduction, anti-inflammatory. Low-dose (75-150mg): Prevention of heart attack, stroke, and blood clots.
side_effects: Common: Stomach upset, heartburn, nausea. Serious: GI bleeding, peptic ulcers, tinnitus (ringing in ears), Reye's syndrome in children, allergic reactions (aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease), increased bleeding.
dosage: Pain/Fever: 325-650mg every 4-6 hours. Cardioprotection: 75-150mg once daily.
warnings: Do NOT give to children under 16 (Reye's syndrome risk). Stop 7 days before surgery. Caution in asthma (may trigger bronchospasm).
interactions: Anticoagulants, methotrexate, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, valproic acid, corticosteroids.

uses: Inflammatory conditions (arthritis, asthma, allergies, skin conditions), autoimmune diseases (lupus, multiple sclerosis), organ transplant rejection prevention, severe allergic reactions.
side_effects: Short-term: Increased appetite, mood changes, insomnia, stomach upset. Long-term: Weight gain, osteoporosis, diabetes, cataracts, adrenal suppression, skin thinning, increased infection risk, moon face, muscle weakness.
dosage: Varies widely by condition. Usually 5-60mg daily. Taper gradually - do not stop suddenly.
warnings: NEVER stop suddenly after prolonged use (adrenal crisis). Increases infection risk. Monitor blood sugar. May mask signs of infection. Carry steroid card.
interactions: NSAIDs, warfarin, diabetes medications, diuretics, vaccines (avoid live vaccines), CYP3A4 inducers.
available_forms: Tablet (5mg, 10mg, 20mg), Oral solution, Injection, Eye drops

uses: Urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, skin infections, bone and joint infections, gastrointestinal infections, anthrax exposure.
side_effects: Common: Nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, headache. Serious: Tendon rupture (especially Achilles), peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects (seizures, confusion), QT prolongation, aortic dissection, C. difficile colitis. FDA BLACK BOX WARNING for tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects.
dosage: Adults: 250-750mg every 12 hours depending on infection.
warnings: FDA BLACK BOX WARNING: Risk of tendon rupture, neuropathy. Avoid in myasthenia gravis. Not first-line for UTI if alternatives available. Avoid excessive sun exposure.
interactions: Antacids/calcium/iron (take 2 hours apart), theophylline, warfarin, tizanidine (contraindicated), NSAIDs.

uses: Previously used for acid reflux (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. IMPORTANT: Ranitidine was withdrawn from many markets in 2020 due to NDMA (a probable carcinogen) contamination concerns.
side_effects: Common: Headache, dizziness, diarrhea, constipation. NDMA contamination risk with storage.
dosage: Not recommended due to withdrawal. Use alternatives like famotidine.
warnings: WITHDRAWN FROM MARKET in many countries due to carcinogen (NDMA) contamination. Ask your doctor for alternative H2 blockers like famotidine or PPIs.
interactions: Ketoconazole, atazanavir, gefitinib.

uses: High blood pressure (hypertension), heart failure, post-myocardial infarction, diabetic nephropathy.
side_effects: Common: Dry cough (10-15% of patients), dizziness, headache, fatigue. Serious: Angioedema (swelling of face/tongue - emergency), hyperkalemia, kidney impairment, hypotension.
dosage: Adults: Start 10mg once daily for hypertension. Range 5-40mg daily.
warnings: Do NOT use in pregnancy. Stop if angioedema occurs. Monitor potassium and kidney function. Higher angioedema risk in Black patients.
interactions: Potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, lithium, aliskiren.
manufacturer: Various (Prinivil by Merck, Zestril by AstraZeneca)

uses: Moderate to moderately severe pain in adults.
side_effects: Common: Nausea, dizziness, constipation, headache, drowsiness, vomiting. Serious: Seizures, serotonin syndrome, respiratory depression, dependence/addiction, withdrawal symptoms.
dosage: Adults: 50-100mg every 4-6 hours as needed. Maximum 400mg/day.
warnings: Risk of addiction and dependence. May cause seizures especially at high doses. Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs/SNRIs. NOT for children under 12. Schedule IV controlled substance.
interactions: MAO inhibitors (contraindicated), SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclic antidepressants, carbamazepine, warfarin.

uses: Community-acquired pneumonia, hospital-acquired pneumonia, complicated urinary tract infections, acute sinusitis, chronic bronchitis exacerbation, skin infections, plague, anthrax.
side_effects: Common: Nausea, headache, diarrhea, insomnia, dizziness. Serious: Tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity. FDA BLACK BOX WARNING same as ciprofloxacin.
dosage: Adults: 250-750mg once daily for 5-14 days depending on infection.
warnings: Same black box warnings as ciprofloxacin. Not first-line for sinusitis or bronchitis if alternatives exist. Photosensitivity - avoid sun.
interactions: Antacids/iron/calcium (take 2 hours apart), warfarin, NSAIDs, theophylline, antidiabetic agents.

uses: Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes mellitus for blood sugar control.
side_effects: Common: Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), injection site reactions, weight gain. Serious: Severe hypoglycemia, lipodystrophy at injection sites, allergic reactions.
dosage: Individualized. Type 2: Start 10 units once daily. Adjust based on blood glucose monitoring.
warnings: Never share insulin pens. Monitor blood sugar regularly. Does NOT cover mealtime blood sugar spikes (need rapid-acting insulin for that). Do not mix with other insulins.
interactions: Other antidiabetic drugs (increased hypoglycemia risk), beta-blockers (mask hypoglycemia symptoms), corticosteroids, thiazide diuretics.

uses: Acute asthma attacks (rescue inhaler), exercise-induced bronchospasm, COPD symptom relief, bronchospasm prevention.
side_effects: Common: Tremor, headache, palpitations, tachycardia, nervousness. Uncommon: Muscle cramps, hypokalemia, dizziness.
dosage: Inhaler: 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed. For acute attacks: 2-4 puffs, may repeat every 20 minutes for up to 3 doses.
warnings: This is a RESCUE inhaler - if using more than 2 days/week, asthma is not well controlled. Seek medical help if no relief. May increase heart rate.
interactions: Beta-blockers (may reduce effectiveness), diuretics (increased hypokalemia risk), MAO inhibitors, digoxin.

uses: Nausea and vomiting, bloating, feeling of fullness, gastroparesis, acid reflux symptoms.
side_effects: Common: Dry mouth, headache, diarrhea. Serious: QT prolongation, cardiac arrhythmias (especially at high doses or in elderly), galactorrhea (breast milk production), menstrual irregularities.
dosage: Adults: 10mg up to 3 times daily before meals. Maximum 30mg/day. Use for shortest duration needed.
warnings: Risk of cardiac arrhythmias - avoid in patients with QT prolongation, heart disease. Not available in the US (restricted by FDA). Use lowest effective dose for shortest time.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin - contraindicated), QT-prolonging drugs.

uses: Vaginal candidiasis (yeast infection), oral thrush, esophageal candidiasis, cryptococcal meningitis, systemic fungal infections, prevention of fungal infections in immunocompromised patients.
side_effects: Common: Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea. Serious: Liver damage (hepatotoxicity), QT prolongation, severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson), adrenal insufficiency.
dosage: Vaginal candidiasis: Single dose 150mg. Oral thrush: 200mg day 1, then 100mg daily for 7-14 days.
warnings: Monitor liver function with prolonged use. QT prolongation risk. Drug interactions are extensive.
interactions: Warfarin (increased bleeding), statins (rhabdomyolysis risk), midazolam, cisapride (contraindicated), phenytoin, cyclosporine.
